## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Tatiyabodhi Sutta* (Ud 1.3; PTS Ud 2), also titled *Tatiyabodhisutta*, is the third discourse of the *Bodhivagga* in the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. Set shortly after the Buddha's awakening, the sutta describes the Buddha contemplating specific conditionality and dependent co-arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) in both direct and reverse orders, concluding with an inspired utterance (*udāna*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records seventeen translations in fourteen languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the first chapter of the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra* (SF 259), and verses in various recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 33, UVS 33, Tibetan Uv Kg 33, and Chinese T 212.34 and T 213.33) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling narrative episodes occur in the *Mahāvastu* (Mvu 17, 91) and the companion *Paṭhamabodhi* and *Dutiyabodhi* suttas (Ud 1.1, Ud 1.2), while the text is also cited in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.3) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus matches confirm dense Pali-internal text reuse involving the dependent origination formulas and conclusion verses, sharing major segments with the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), the *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the sutta with Sanskrit and Tibetan canonical texts treating the awakening narrative and dependent arising, including the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-4), the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the *Lalitavistara*, the *Śālistambasūtra*, and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
